findings.diagnosis: The prompt underestimates contra risk for prefixes that stop inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses or before a clause‑finishing verb/qualification: it lets cuts that leave an asserted prefix which the remainder then negates or qualifies (contra≈1) survive.
findings.evidence: de_de_86, de_de_240, de_de_958, de_de_648, de_de_587, de_de_594 — all show the policy keeping a cut that leaves a subordinate or qualifying clause unfinished and that cut has very high measured contra; the offline target removes or moves that cut.

edit.text: If a cut would end inside a subordinate/verb‑final clause or before the clause’s finishing verb that supplies a qualification or reversal, treat the prefix as high contradiction risk (score the cut very low).

findings.diagnosis: The prompt's warning about determiners/short prepositions is being applied too conservatively in dense (short‑chunk) settings: it discourages early cuts after function words even when short‑latency segmentation requires many small pieces and the split causes only minor cohesion loss.
findings.evidence: de_de_86, de_de_587, de_de_594, de_de_648, de_de_240 — all are in short latency bins where the offline target adds earlier cuts (including after small function words) to achieve much higher H_set; the policy avoided those cuts and lost most of the gap in short bins.

edit.text: When dense segmentation is required, allow cuts immediately after determiners/short prepositions provided they do not separate a head from its required complements; prefer small cohesion loss to failing to produce the needed density.
